title: tier-2 shipped code: the client's 8-byte hex id parser against ParseHexKeyId (0x14248f040)
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/install.rs::parse_hex_key_id (with the same hex_decode, hex_value and leading_whitespace leaves), built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the parse_hex_key_id entry.

Oracle is ParseHexKeyId at exe 0x14248f040, extent 0x14248f040..0x14248f0aa (106 bytes through the ret), which is the declared coverageWindow. Signature: (const char *text, size_t len, u8 out[8], u8 *flag) -> size_t consumed.

The client's read is ParseHexKey's body with an 8-byte target: zero the 8-byte out (one qword store) and `*flag`, skip `0x20`/`0x09..=0x0d`, call 0x14269ab80(out, 8, text + ws, len - ws), and return `ws + 0x10` when exactly 8 bytes decoded, else 0.
Compared channels: the 64-bit return, the read-only text, the 8-byte out block and the 1-byte flag, all pre-filled with 0xA5 so the zeroing and partial writes are visible.
Coverage gate is 100% over the window's sites: the same whitespace and length edges as ParseHexKey at the 8-byte width.

acknowledgedGaps.what: a len larger than the text buffer
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client reads `len` bytes from the pointer it was given; a shorter buffer is a caller bug and would read past the arena. The probe rejects it and the fixture never builds one.

They are inside the call, so they are outside this unit's coverage window; they run in the oracle and their effect is compared through the 16-byte output. 0x14269ab80 has 7 call sites and is a candidate for its own unit.
